title: Fix flaky drain pid-file test by removing its stop-file race
summary: Make status_and_stop_find_the_drain_by_pid_file_when_command_lines_contain_drain deterministic. Working hypothesis: stop_and_wait writes the stop file before it checks the state, and the test's `sh` drain polls that same file every 50 ms. Under load the drain can exit before the "asked only" call checks it, so that call returns NotRunning instead of Asked. The producer must confirm this by reproducing it under load, state the cause and evidence, fix the test, and add a CHANGELOG line. The audience is the maintainers whose checks fail on unrelated jobs.

defaults_applied.how: The fix is Rust test code.
cargo test and clippy must pass.
A 200-run loop under load is recorded.
The cause is reproduced and stated, not hidden with retries or longer timeouts.
Criteria check the test passing in a loop.
Comments and CHANGELOG are written for outside readers.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Code survey: read crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs. The test is at about line 5051. Its helpers are sleeper, record_of, quick and settled (about lines 4968-5012). The code under test is drain_state (3496), stop_and_wait (3696), RealProcs::start_marker and linux_marker (3401-3431). drain_state reads the pid file, then compares the /proc/<pid>/stat start-time field with the recorded value. It never reads the command line, so the decoy is ignored simply because it is not in the pid file. No record or data file is added, so check_record_file, AnyRecord and the round-trip test are not involved. The property is measured directly by running the real test in a loop.

Hypothesised cause: the test's shell loop exits on the stop file within 50 ms. stop_and_wait writes that file and only then calls drain_state. Under CPU contention the shell can exit and become a zombie in that gap. linux_marker then returns None, so the first call returns NotRunning(Dead) rather than Asked, and the assertion fails. The producer must confirm or correct this by reproduction. The fix, if confirmed, changes only the test's synchronisation, for example a drain stand-in that exits only on a second signal file the test creates after the asked-only assertions, while the real stop file is still what is written and checked.
No production code change is expected unless the reproduction shows the cause is in drain.rs non-test code.
Reproduction under load uses cargo test in a loop alongside other cargo tests. The run is recorded as check output.
CHANGELOG.md gets one entry describing only the test change in the diff.

acceptance_criteria.text: The job report states the cause of the flake and the evidence for it: reproduction output under load, plus the code lines involved in crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs.

Run `cargo test -p athena-cli status_and_stop_find_the_drain_by_pid_file_when_command_lines_contain_drain` 200 times in a row while other cargo tests run in parallel. Every run passes, and the recorded check output shows the loop.

In the diff, the test still writes a pid file naming only the real drain child. It still starts a decoy with arg0 'athena drain --budget 9' that is not in the pid file. It still asserts that drain_state returns Running(record), that the status text has the drain pid and not the decoy pid, that the stop outcomes are Asked and then Exited, and that the decoy is still alive at the end.
CHANGELOG.md has an entry that describes only what the diff does, with no claims beyond it.
Run `cargo test -p athena-cli`, `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check`. All pass with no new warnings.
Only crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs and CHANGELOG.md are changed. The change adds no new refusal rule, so no refusal-rate figure applies.

out_of_scope: Changing how drain_state or stop_and_wait detect the drain, unless the reproduction proves the cause is there.
Changes to athena.toml, defaults.toml, workflows or other governance files.
departures: A 200-run loop under load is slow and the cause is unconfirmed, so cost and time are a little above the reference.
urgent_reason: Removes a flaky check that has failed unrelated jobs twice and wasted re-runs, so it cuts rejected attempts and redo work.
